<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **15** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/field.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**11** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-driven.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/external-datasources.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/field-types.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/validation-rules.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/deployment/troubleshooting.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/getting-started/quick-reference.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/protocol/backward-compatibility.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/concept.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-4.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/field.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **182** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ddc96d8a4280c69305dd541005cacfbe3e58f4c5` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `829010ad78a87d7b2b40d676f4c8f2c039c3bc23` — the merge of head `1916ae98dbe07ffc95354785e67ac18107c31501` into base `ddc96d8a4280c69305dd541005cacfbe3e58f4c5`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 829010ad78a87d7b2b40d676f4c8f2c039c3bc23 && git checkout 829010ad78a87d7b2b40d676f4c8f2c039c3bc23
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ddc96d8a4280c69305dd541005cacfbe3e58f4c5 1916ae98dbe07ffc95354785e67ac18107c31501 && git checkout -B drift-repro ddc96d8a4280c69305dd541005cacfbe3e58f4c5 && git merge --no-ff 1916ae98dbe07ffc95354785e67ac18107c31501

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ddc96d8a4280c69305dd541005cacfbe3e58f4c5
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ddc96d8a4280c69305dd541005cacfbe3e58f4c5` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `17cf9c93adae9a98dd99a0b29dd58be29f00c82e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/field.metadata-form.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts + packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts, packages/spec/liveness/field.json, packages/qa/dogfood/test/expression-conformance.ledger.ts, ui/packages/core/src/evaluator/handLock.ts, ui/packages/plugin-gantt/src/ganttHandLock.ts, ui/packages/plugin-gantt/src/ObjectGantt.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-timesheet/src/timesheetModel.ts, ui/packages/plugin-timesheet/src/ObjectTimesheet.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/chrome/paletteCreate.ts, ui/packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx

Read: card #37448 (body and its five comments), the PR body and file list, the net diff against `main`, and the check-runs on the head (every one `success` or `skipped`; none failed). Code outside the diff was read in the head's tree to judge the texts, not reviewed. The tests, the generated locale bundles, the reference pages and the changeset prose are the lane seat's ACCEPT.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set: unchanged — right.** `FieldSchema` gains and loses no key and no value; only `.describe` and JSDoc text moves in `field.zod.ts`, and two `helpText` strings in `field.metadata-form.ts`. The generated bundles and `content/docs/references/data/field.mdx` follow those strings.
- **Public surface: one additive change — right under `Clause-②: no`, with a note.** `cellEditable` (exported from `@object-ui/plugin-timesheet`) takes an optional third parameter whose default keeps the old answer. `ganttHandLock.ts` is not exported from the package index. `PaletteCreateObjectDef.fields` reads one more optional key. No caller breaks.
- **Behaviour: the console refuses hand edits it took on `main` — right, and it is the declared key made real** (ADR-0049, ruling 7180466652 as the card cites it): Gantt bar writes and dependency links, the timesheet cell and its create, the palette prefill. No API, import, action or flow write changes; the engine still never reads either key.
- **"Every console surface" as a derived claim: wrong.** See M1.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: no` — right: no accept set widens and the one signature change is an optional parameter.
- `Metadata-protocol: semantic` where the claim said `none` — **right.** What an author's `uiReadonly: true` / `uiReadonlyWhen` does changes (more surfaces lock) while nothing an author can write is added or refused: a changed meaning, so `semantic`, not `none`, `added` or `narrowed`. `semantic` takes `minor`, and the changeset gives `minor` to `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/platform-objects` and the four UI packages whose behaviour or published text moves. `Check Changeset` is green on the head.
- N1 below covers the one package left at `patch`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Open question (the in-app assistant acting for a person): escalated, not answered here.** The card's own text says the ruling counts the assistant as a hand surface, so option B (leave it out permanently) contradicts the ruling as the card states it and is the maintainer's to give; option A needs a card where the assistant's writes run, outside this repo. `Part of #37448` is the right link and the card stays open. The dev report lists the carrier as "noted, not filed": the seat owes that card, or the surface has no owner.
- **Dev flag, `Metadata-protocol` changed from the claim:** judged in ②, right.
- **N8 (`BEHAVIOUR_SEGMENTS`):** answered with a reason and a pin; the lint source is unchanged and `Test Core` is green. Accepted as an answer; the pin is the lane seat's.
- **N7 (ledger row):** reworded; the new sentence agrees with the head (the edit dialog and the grid cell call `resolveFieldRuleState`, the other hosts go through `fieldReadOnlyByHand`).
- **SQL push-down:** no new id materialisation and no in-app join. `ListView` adds the detected lane field's lock operands to the `$select` it already sends. The Gantt and timesheet reads are unchanged.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts`** — the `uiReadonly` describe and JSDoc now say the lock holds on "every console surface" and name the assistant as the one exception. The surfaces the text lists are each true of the head: the Gantt gate sits in `handleTaskUpdateDefault` and `persistDependencies`, the only two record writes of the chart (the drawer goes through `RecordDetailPanel`, which reads the verdict); the timesheet judges the cell at draw and again at commit; the palette reads the static half. The assistant sentence is true. The universal is not:

M1 (must-fix) — **the calendar's quick-create dialog writes a hand-locked field, so "every console surface" is false of the head.** `ui/packages/plugin-calendar/src/ObjectCalendar.tsx` `submitQuickCreate` builds its payload from the title field, `quickCreateDateValues` (the start and end date fields) and `quickCreateFill` (a value for each other required field), and sends it with `dataSource.create`. None of the three reads `uiReadonly`: the dialog is gated by `calendarQuickCreate` (the create grant) and by `requiredFieldsQuickCreateCannotFill`, which exempts `readonly` only. `startFieldLocked` / `endFieldLocked` close the drag and the resize handle, not the day click or the range select. So on an object whose calendar start field (or title field) is `uiReadonly: true`, a person clicks a day, types a title, and the console create carries the locked field; and a `required` + `uiReadonly` select with no `defaultValue` is written with its first option, where the describe says such a create fails. That contradicts three sentences this PR publishes or keeps: "every console surface", "the create and edit dialogs (it is left off them and out of their payload)" read as the console's creates, and "A console create leaves the field out and the server applies its `defaultValue`". The PR judges two other creates by the static half (timesheet, palette), so this one is the same class left out. The file is not in the diff; the finding is against the text. Fix either side: judge the quick-create by the static half (leave a locked field out of the payload and out of `quickCreateFill`, or hand the gesture to the full form) with a pin, or narrow the texts to the surfaces that hold. The same sentence is in the `uiReadonly` JSDoc, the `field.json` note ("Honoured on every console surface"), the changeset and the surfaces below.

**`packages/spec/src/data/field.metadata-form.ts`** — "anywhere in the console" in both help texts carries M1. The `uiReadonlyWhen` text is otherwise right: a create is not judged, so M1 does not reach its conditional half.

**`packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts` (`describe_object`)** — "a person cannot edit the field on any console surface" carries M1, and:

S1 (should-fix) — **`describe_object` and the two help texts state the universal without the open surface, and the PR body says otherwise.** The body says the `describe_object` guidance "name[s] the assistant as the one that does not yet"; the tree's text does not mention it, and its code comment says "every console surface honours the hand lock". The reader of this text is an agent. "Your write may still set it" is right for an API caller, and is the opposite of the ruling for the in-app assistant acting for a person, which the card counts as a hand surface. While that surface is open the text should say so in one clause, as the `uiReadonly` describe does; the help texts either gain the same clause or stop at the surfaces they list.

**Implementing files, against the contract:**

- `ganttHandLock.ts` / `ObjectGantt.tsx` — agree. The verdict is judged over the stored record with the shell's scope; a changed locked field refuses the patch, an echoed one is dropped; the static half only narrows the authored switches. A stored date that is not a string and is echoed back is refused rather than dropped, which fails closed.
- `timesheetModel.ts` / `ObjectTimesheet.tsx` — agree. The create is judged by the static half over the row, date and value fields; the one-record cell by the full verdict, at draw and at commit.
- `paletteCreate.ts`, `ListView.tsx`, `handLock.ts` header, the ledger row — agree with the head.

N1 (nit) — the changeset leaves `@object-ui/core` at `patch` beside a `semantic` declaration; the rule's letter gives a moved package `minor`. The diff to that package is a comment and the gate is green.

N2 (nit) — `field.json` cites `timesheetModel.ts#cellEditable` as the timesheet reader of `uiReadonlyWhen`. That function takes the verdict as a callback whose default answers open; the read of the key is `valueLockedByHand` in `ObjectTimesheet.tsx`.

Nothing private.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-riww1b`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L6bhgV6i8jfWwSXjpWJrjA`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `1916ae98dbe07ffc95354785e67ac18107c31501`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/field.metadata-form.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts + ui/packages/plugin-calendar/src/ObjectCalendar.tsx, packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts, packages/spec/liveness/field.json, ui/packages/core/src/evaluator/handLock.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/expression-conformance.ledger.ts, ui/packages/plugin-gantt/src/ganttHandLock.ts, ui/packages/plugin-gantt/src/ObjectGantt.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-timesheet/src/timesheetModel.ts, ui/packages/plugin-timesheet/src/ObjectTimesheet.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/chrome/paletteCreate.ts, ui/packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx

Delta round on record 7214835610 (FAIL at `17cf9c93`). Read: card #37448 (body and its five comments), the PR body and file list, record 7214835610, the net diff against `main`, the two PR-side commits after `17cf9c93` (`fcf111d7ab`, `f116031585`) and the merge commit, and the check-runs on the head (every one `success` or `skipped`; none failed). Code outside the diff was read in the head's tree to judge the texts, not reviewed. The tests (the new calendar pin included), the generated locale bundles, the reference pages and the changeset prose are the lane seat's ACCEPT.

**The merge brings only `main`'s content.** The head is a two-parent merge of `f116031585` with `ddc96d8a42`, which is an ancestor of `main`. Git's re-merge of the two parents reproduces the merge tree exactly (no conflict resolution and no hand edit in the merge), and the diff from the `main` parent to the head is byte-identical to the PR's net diff (36 files). Files the gantt, timesheet, palette, list and ledger rows of the scope name are unchanged since `17cf9c93`; the earlier record's reading of them stands and is not repeated.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set: unchanged — right.** The delta moves `.describe`, JSDoc and `helpText` strings only in the two `hits` files; `FieldSchema` gains and loses no key and no value.
- **Public surface: nothing new in the delta — right.** `ObjectCalendar.tsx` gains two module-private helpers and one optional key on a private interface; no export changes.
- **Behaviour: the calendar quick-create no longer writes a statically hand-locked field — right, and it is the declared key made real.** Three new effects, each judged right: (a) a title, start or end field that is `uiReadonly: true` sends the day click and the range drag to the host's full create form, with a locked date field left out of the prefill, and offers nothing when there is no host form; (b) a `required` + `uiReadonly` field is left out of the dialog's write, so the server applies its `defaultValue`; (c) one with no `defaultValue` counts as unfillable and the gesture is handed off.
- **One effect wider than the card, right:** the static half also answers true for `readonly: true`, so a calendar whose title or date field is server-locked now hands off as well, where `main` opened the dialog and the server dropped the field on insert. That was a dialog writing a value the server discards; the hand-off is the stricter and more honest answer. See N3.
- **"Every console surface, the assistant excepted" as a derived claim: right on this head**, as far as it can be read. Beyond the surfaces the earlier record walked, the record writes under `ui/packages` reachable by a person were re-read: the console's form renderers (drawer, modal, tabbed, wizard) build their write through the one sanitiser that reads the static half; the calendar and kanban drawers save through the record panel that reads the verdict; the grid's bulk executor runs authored actions, which the ruling keeps. No further hand surface was found writing a locked field; this is a reading of the write call sites, not a proof of the universal.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: no` — right: no accept set widens and no exported signature changes in the delta.
- `Metadata-protocol: semantic` where the claim said `none` — right, as judged in 7214835610: what an author's `uiReadonly` / `uiReadonlyWhen` does changes (more surfaces lock) while nothing an author can write is added or refused. The delta adds one more such surface and does not change the level.
- The changeset now gives `@object-ui/plugin-calendar` `minor`, which the calendar change needs. `Check Changeset` is green on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Open question (the in-app assistant acting for a person): escalated, with a carrier.** `Part of #37448` stays the right link. The seat notes name card #37898 as the carrier of the surface; that card is outside this round's inputs and was not read. Which of the dev's options A or B holds is still the maintainer's to give.
- **Dev flag, `Metadata-protocol` changed from the claim:** judged in ②, right.
- **Dev flag, N1 deliberately left:** accepted as a deviation, below.
- **N7, N8:** unchanged since 7214835610; answered there.
- **SQL push-down:** the delta adds no read at all. No new id materialisation and no in-app join.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

M1: closed. `submitQuickCreate` in `ui/packages/plugin-calendar/src/ObjectCalendar.tsx` is now reachable only when `quickCreateLockedOwnFields` is empty, so the title and date keys it writes are never statically locked; its required-field loop skips a statically locked field before `quickCreateFill`, so the first-option write the earlier record named is gone; and `requiredFieldsQuickCreateCannotFill` counts a required locked field with no `defaultValue` as unfillable, so the dialog is not offered for a write the describe says fails. Tried to break it: fields authored as an array (both helpers read through `quickCreateFieldEntries`, so the lock is found); the default title key `name`; an end field locked alone (hand-off, end left out of the prefill, start kept); a caller-supplied `onDateClick` (the caller's own handler, not this component's write); no `onEdit` (no affordance, never a dialog that writes). Each holds. The three sentences M1 cited are true of the head: "every console surface", "left off them and out of their payload", and "A console create leaves the field out and the server applies its `defaultValue`".

S1: closed. The `describe_object` description now reads "a person cannot edit the field on any console surface, though the in-app assistant acting for a person does not honour it yet", and its code comment says the same; both help texts in `field.metadata-form.ts` end with "The in-app assistant acting for a person does not honour it yet." The universal no longer stands without its exception on any of the three.

**`packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts`** — holds. The `uiReadonly` describe and JSDoc list "calendar drag and quick-create" and keep the assistant sentence; each listed surface is true of the head. The `uiReadonlyWhen` describe correctly does NOT gain quick-create: a create is judged by the static half only, and the text says "A create is not judged". It leaves the assistant exception to `uiReadonly` by reference ("see `uiReadonly`"), which is enough.

**`packages/spec/src/data/field.metadata-form.ts`** — holds. "Anywhere in the console" is now true of the tree with the trailing exception. The parenthesis says "calendar and Gantt drag" and does not name quick-create; it is an illustration under a universal that holds, not a closed list.

**Implementing files in the delta, against the contract:**

- `ObjectCalendar.tsx` — agrees, sentence by sentence, as under M1.
- `mcp-http-tools.ts` — agrees. "Your write may still set it, judged by the validations" stays right for an API caller, and the reader now learns the assistant is the open surface.
- `field.json` — agrees. The `uiReadonly` evidence cites "calendar drag and quick-create"; the `uiReadonlyWhen` evidence now cites `ObjectTimesheet.tsx#valueLockedByHand`, which exists on the head and is the read of the key.
- `handLock.ts` header — agrees with the head.

N1: left as is by the dev (`@object-ui/core` at `patch` beside a `semantic` declaration; the diff to that package is a comment and the gate is green). Accepted deviation.

N2: fixed on a prose face, as above.

N3 (nit) — the changeset's calendar bullet and the PR body speak of a field "locked by hand" and do not say that a server-locked (`readonly: true`) title or date field now hands the gesture off too; and the PR body's summary, "What changes" and "Verification" sections predate the delta (no calendar quick-create, head `17cf9c93`). Prose only; the PR body can be brought up to date without moving the head.

Nothing private.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-riww1b`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L6bhgV6i8jfWwSXjpWJrjA`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · head 1916ae98db · card #37448 · area s2-data · 2026-11-27T10:39Z

**L1 checklist**
- **Shape and checks.** Every check on the head is green; the one `cancelled` Check Changeset run was superseded by the rerun after the body edit, which succeeded. The two published packages the diff touches without a changeset entry, `@objectstack/lint` and `@object-ui/plugin-kanban`, move a test file each (`validate-field-consumers.test.ts`, `ObjectKanban.handLock-36806.test.tsx`), which does not ship.
- **Contract review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`.** 7214835610 at `17cf9c93` was FAIL (M1 calendar quick-create wrote hand-locked fields; S1 texts did not name the assistant). The delta record 7215978601 at this head: PASS, `No must-fix, no should-fix.`; `M1: closed` in code (the quick-create is offered only when its own title and date fields are not statically locked, a locked required field is skipped or hands off), `S1: closed`, N2 fixed, N1 an accepted deviation, N3 (PR body) fixed in the body without moving the head. Its transcript passes `verify-review-tier`. The seat adopts it.
- **Merge of `main`.** Brings only `main`'s own content: the record finds the second parent an ancestor of `main` and the PR's net diff byte-identical to the head against its `main` parent.
- **Declarations.** `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: semantic` (the declared lock now locks more surfaces) on the body and the changeset; `@object-ui/plugin-calendar` at `minor`. `Skills-docs: none` — no page under `skills/**` teaches `uiReadonly` or the hand lock, read on `main`.
- **`Part of #37448` is right.** One surface stays open, the in-app assistant writing for a person, now card #37898. #37448 keeps `pm:dispatched` until the remaining surface lands.
- **Governance.** `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 37888` on this file list: NOT governed, 873 changed lines (under the human-merge threshold). The contract face is answered by the at-tier record above.

Tier: S. Landing: ready and auto-merge in this stroke.
